one_liner: Federal contracting officer-track job buying IT products and services for DISA: soliciting, evaluating, negotiating, pricing and administering Defense contracts at Fort Meade.
fit_summary: This job hinges on hands-on procurement experience (pre- and post-award work, price or cost analysis, market research reports or performance work statements). Daniel's proposal research and writing at IEM (2019 to 2024) and his medical-supply purchasing for vaccination sites give him working knowledge of solicitations, so GS-9 is worth trying. The posting's education substitute at GS-9 is a master's in a listed field such as business, law, economics or accounting, so it is unclear whether his Global Affairs M.A. counts. GS-11 and 12 need federal contracting experience he doesn't have.
eligibility: Open to the public under DoD Direct Hire Authority (5 U.S.C. 9905); no federal status is needed and veterans' preference does not apply.
A bachelor's degree is mandatory for the 1102 series. His M.A. (George Mason, 2016) implies one; list the bachelor's on the resume, since the posting says not to send transcripts.

GS-9 requires one year of specialized experience at GS-7 level: pre- or post-award procurement functions, price or cost analysis for contract actions, or drafting procurement documents such as market research reports or performance work statements. Alternatively, a master's degree or two years of graduate study in a listed field such as business, law, economics or accounting substitutes.
GS-11 requires one year awarding or administering federal contracts or doing price/cost analysis, and GS-12 requires experience in all phases of federal procurement.
A Secret clearance is required; expect a background investigation after selection.
strategy: Target GS-9 and be honest with yourself about GS-11/12: those grades require you to have actually awarded or administered federal contracts.

Describe the contractor-side work in the posting's terms: market research on SAM.gov, GovWin and DHS forecasts, reading solicitations and statements of work, writing proposals, and buying and tracking supplies. Claim only what he did, and mention the economics and trade coursework in his M.A. in case HR weighs it.
State the specialized experience explicitly in the body of the resume, since the posting requires it there. Within the two-page limit, include month/year dates and hours per week for each job.
Show the four competencies (Attention to Detail, Influencing/Negotiating, Decision Making, Reasoning) with brief concrete examples from client work.
Follow the application instructions exactly: email the resume to disa.meade.psd.mbx.psd-1102-applications@mail.mil with "Announcement 12997520" in the subject line. Do not send transcripts.
The announcement is open from 2026-07-09 to 2027-01-08 and direct hire moves quickly, so apply early rather than waiting for the close date.
resume_bullets: Found multimillion-dollar opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin, BidPro and the DHS acquisition forecast, and led proposal writing in answer to government solicitations (2019–2024).
As part of the logistics team, procured medical supplies, equipment and vaccines for COVID-19 sites in six states, and set up relationships with medical supply and truck rental vendors (2021–2022).
Tracked orders and spending in Excel pivot-table reports for the logistics team.
interview_questions: Walk us through a procurement document you drafted, such as a market research report or PWS, and how you made sure it was accurate.
How would you evaluate whether a contractor's proposed price is fair and reasonable?
Describe a time you negotiated with or influenced stakeholders who had competing interests.
What is the difference between fixed-price and cost-type contracts, and when is each appropriate?
watch_outs: A bachelor's degree is required for new 1102 entrants. He meets it through his degrees, but the resume should list the bachelor's, not only the M.A.
Pure policy, outreach or emergency-planning work will not count as specialized experience, so Daniel needs real procurement or pricing duties to qualify.
The job is at Fort Meade, MD, a long commute from Manassas; telework is available but the role is not remote.
A Secret clearance is required, and the role involves technical IT acquisition and cost analysis that may suit Daniel's public-facing strengths less than policy or legislative roles.
